messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — planning canary rollout for rerank endpoint schema v2 tomorrow 9am PT. Need a couple quick decisions on tie-breaking and backward-compat behavior before I ship the docs.
aj: Which fields are changing? Will older clients fail?
maria: Minimal shape change. We keep `items[]` and `score` but add optional metadata: `stable_sort_id` (string) and `tie_hint` (float). Also adding top-level `compat_mode` query flag for rolling clients.
ken: Can we keep default behavior identical when new fields are absent? Important for old clients.
maria: Yes — default: if `stable_sort_id` missing, fallback to original insertion order. If `score` missing or null -> treat as -Inf (send to bottom). If `tie_hint` present, use it only when scores equal within epsilon.
sam: For deterministic ties we still need a hash fallback so order doesn't flip across replicas. Proposal: compute `tie_hash = hash(stable_sort_id || id || request_id || item_index)` and sort by that as last resort.
lina: That sounds fine. Two small q's: 1) what epsilon for score equality? 2) does `tie_hint` override hash?
maria: 1) epsilon = 1e-6 for floats. 2) `tie_hint` has higher precedence than hash but lower than explicit `stable_sort_id`. Order: score desc -> tie_hint desc -> stable_sort_id asc (lex) -> tie_hash asc.
aj: Nice. For docs/sample payload can you add a quick example I can share with partners?
maria: Sure — sample response:
```json
{
  "request_id": "req_123",
  "items": [
    {"id": "A", "score": 0.87, "stable_sort_id": "202301-A", "tie_hint": 0.1},
    {"id": "B", "score": 0.87, "stable_sort_id": null, "tie_hint": 0.05},
    {"id": "C", "score": 0.42}
  ]
}
```
ken: Ok. One more: what about NaN in `score` from some models? We had previous outages when clients returned NaN.
maria: Treat NaN as null (=> -Inf). We'll also log and emit eval alerts when NaN rate > 0.1%.
sam: Do we need a compatibility header instead of query flag? Some infra prefers header toggles.
maria: Good point — we'll support both `X-Compat-Mode: v1` header and `?compat_mode=v1`. Server favors header if both present.
deposit-bot: (typo) — ignore
deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: rerank-service v2 on canary pool at 2024-05-10T16:00:00Z.
lina: Awesome. Who's taking code review for the schema PR?\maria: @ken can you take the schema + server changes? @sam pls own docs + migration guide. I'll do the rollout plan and alerting dashboards.
ken: I'll review this morning, ping me with the PR link.
sam: Will update the docs and add a short migration checklist for partners. Also will add a note to the changelog about stable_sort_id semantics.
aj: Small ask — can we include an example client snippet for stable ordering in SDKs? saves partner confusion.
maria: Agree. Sam can add it to SDK examples. Action items: ken - review PR; sam - docs + examples; maria - rollout + alerts; lina - smoke test after canary.
lina: Happy to smoke test.
maria: Thanks all. If no objections I'll merge schema PR today EOD and schedule canary.
ken: No objections from me.
sam: 👍
aj: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary started on pool canary-3 at 2024-05-10T16:01:15Z. Logs: https://logs.internal/canary-3/2234567890
maria: Lina, ping me when smoke test done and I'll promote to wider pool.
lina: Smoke done — looks good on latency + correctness for 500 samples. No NaNs seen.
maria: Promoting to staged rollout now. Will update thread with final timeline and deprecation window for old clients (2 weeks).
